themes_detail.label: Curb Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 25 THIS WEEK, a 285% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 6.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.7), suggesting rapid street infrastructure degradation across Park Slope/Carroll Gardens that may indicate deferred maintenance or weather-related damage.
evidence: 25 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
285% spike with z-score of 4.7 (high statistical significance)
Concurrent spike in dead/dying tree complaints (6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 avg) and street condition complaints (547 total over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Walking inspection of curbs in Park Slope and Carroll Gardens to document visible damage; interview residents about pedestrian safety hazards
Contact NYC DOT to determine root cause: deferred maintenance budget cuts, winter weather impact, or increased report rate; ask about repair timelines

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged 1900% THIS WEEK with 5 complaints versus a baseline of 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.97), the highest-severity spike in the dataset, likely driven by seasonal expansion of street-seating programs or quality-of-life friction.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
1900% increase with z-score of 10.97 (extreme statistical anomaly, highest in dataset)
Aligns with spring/early summer seasonal reopening of outdoor seating on Prospect Park West, Seventh Avenue, and Carroll Street
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners on Prospect Park West and Seventh Avenue about specific complaints: trash accumulation, noise, table placement, sidewalk obstruction
Obtain 311 complaint details to identify which restaurants/blocks are generating complaints; contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about enforcement actions

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Assistance Requests Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped 450% LAST WEEK with 22 complaints versus a baseline of 4.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.05), indicating either a sudden encampment influx or heightened resident reporting of visible homelessness in parks and transit areas.
evidence: 22 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
450% spike with z-score of 3.05 (high statistical significance)
Aligns with repeated community board budget requests for 'services for the homeless' (Agency: Department of Homeless Services), suggesting chronic unmet need now manifesting as acute complaints
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints by location (Prospect Park, subway stations, street encampments) to identify hotspots; conduct field reporting in those zones
Interview Department of Homeless Services and Parks Enforcement Patrol about outreach capacity; speak with affected residents and business owners about visible encampments and safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Street & Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints increased 161% LAST WEEK with 45 complaints versus a baseline of 17.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.39), alongside concurrent spikes in taxi complaints (500%) and for-hire vehicle complaints (DOWN 68%), suggesting disruption from transit, street vendors, or outdoor activity.
evidence: 45 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 17.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
161% spike with z-score of 3.39 (high statistical significance)
Taxi complaints also up 500% (3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 avg), suggesting transit-related congestion and horn use rather than residential noise alone
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks/corridors generated complaints; stake out during peak hours to document noise sources (taxi congestion, outdoor dining setup, delivery trucks)
Interview NYPD about taxi enforcement and noise complaint response; contact Department of Transportation about traffic signal timing and congestion management on major avenues

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints spiked 433% THIS WEEK with 6 complaints versus a baseline of 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.63), alongside elevated overall damaged tree complaints (333 over 90 days), suggesting disease, pest infestation, or winter damage affecting the neighborhood's canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
433% spike with z-score of 4.63 (high statistical significance)
Damaged tree complaints total 333 over 90-day period; community board has repeated requests to 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' (Department of Parks)
reporting_angles: Walk Prospect Park and residential blocks to photograph dead/dying trees; consult NYC Parks arborist about disease/pest diagnosis (e.g., Asian longhorned beetle, emerald ash borer)
Request Department of Parks tree inventory and treatment records; interview residents about tree loss impact on block character and property values
